goal:
Build ONE file: index.html at the repo root. Self-contained — inline CSS in a <style> block, no build step, no framework, no npm, no bundler, no external CSS/JS/font requests. Deployable by dropping one file on a static host.

This is the public landing page for Voice Tutor. Its ONLY conversion action is an email signup. It must NOT link to the app and must not contain any access token.

DO NOT MODIFY verify.mjs, README.md, or .gitignore. verify.mjs is the frozen acceptance contract, not part of the work. Run it with: node verify.mjs

POSITIONING
Voice Tutor is a voice-based study tool. You upload a document, talk through it out loud, and it steers the conversation and tracks which of the document's claims you've actually covered. Hands-free — designed to be used walking, phone in pocket.
Committed differentiator, do not soften: no flashcards, no decks, no quizzes. Competitors generate cards. Voice Tutor deliberately does not.
Audience: people who need material IN THEIR HEAD, not just findable in their notes — exams, interviews, a new domain at work, or something they genuinely want to understand. Deliberately includes motivated self-learners with no formal deadline. Deliberately EXCLUDES note-taking hobbyists and productivity-system builders. Write NOTHING about vaults, capture, tagging, or knowledge management.
Primary tagline, use verbatim: "No cards. No quizzes. No flashcards. Just a conversation."
NEVER use the phrase "AI-native".

REQUIRED SECTIONS — exactly six <section> elements with these ids, in this document order:
1. id="hero" — headline, one-sentence subhead, the tagline, email form. Lead on the OUTCOME (studying without reading; studying on a walk), not the technology.
2. id="how-it-works" — three steps, one line each: upload a document -> talk through it out loud -> see what you actually covered.
3. id="different" — the no-cards commitment, and hands-free use (works with the phone in your pocket; card-based tools need your eyes and hands). Two short blocks. NO comparison table.
4. id="who" — concrete cases per the audience note above. One short paragraph.
5. id="disclosure" — honest disclosure: early solo project; runs on a machine in the builder's apartment; uploaded documents and conversation transcripts are stored there and the builder reads them; voice passes through third-party speech and AI services. Plain and unapologetic, in the body of the page at full size. It is a TRUST ASSET, not fine print — not a footer, not a modal, not small text.
6. id="signup" — repeat of the form.

THE FORM (appears in both #hero and #signup)
Two fields, each with a proper <label for=...>:
- Email (required)
- "What's the one document you're trying to get into your head right now?" (optional, free text, single line). This is the qualifying question — label it in plain language.
Every input element must have a unique id and an associated <label for="that-id">. Since the form appears twice, ids must be unique across the page.

SUPABASE
Submit via fetch to the Supabase REST API.
Declare EXACTLY these two named constants, once each, at the top of the script, with these exact values:
  const SUPABASE_URL = "https://vxslotmvmuwxlixutvbi.supabase.co";
  const SUPABASE_KEY = "sb_publishable_kAeVtbJztjtIMdPxyOKIiw_SjemghWX";
Endpoint: SUPABASE_URL + "/rest/v1/signups". POST with headers apikey and Content-Type: application/json. Body: { email, document }.
Table columns: id (uuid, auto), email (text, not null), document (text), created_at (auto).

THE KEY IS PUBLIC BY DESIGN and belongs in client code. Do NOT add obfuscation, encoding, base64, string-splitting, or any scheme that pretends otherwise. Write it as a plain string literal. An insert-only RLS policy is what protects the list.
NEVER reference the service-role key. The string "service_role" must appear nowhere.

Behaviour:
- Insert-succeeds-but-select-denied is EXPECTED and correct. A successful insert returns 201 with an EMPTY body. Treat that as success. Do NOT read the row back, do not add select=*, do not parse the response body as the success signal — check response.ok / status only.
- Success and error states render INLINE without navigating away.
- On network or API failure, show a plain message with a mailto: fallback so a motivated person can still reach the builder.
- Basic client-side email format check before submitting, with a clear inline error. Do not block on anything else.
- The submit button must be set disabled BEFORE the fetch call and re-enabled on the failure path, so a double-click cannot double-insert.
- Use a real catch block.

CONSTRAINTS
- One file. System font stack only. The Supabase REST call is the ONLY outbound request the page makes. No other http(s) URL may appear anywhere in the file — not in comments, not in links.
- No analytics, no trackers, no cookie banner.
- Mobile-first. Must read well at 375px, and must not overflow horizontally at 375, 768, or 1280px.
- Semantic HTML, labels tied to inputs, visible focus states, adequate contrast, keyboard navigable.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme (support both light and dark).
- Under 50KB.
- No stock photography, no illustration placeholders, no lorem ipsum. CSS only if a visual is needed.
- No fake social proof — no logos, testimonials, user counts, "trusted by". There are no users yet.
- No manufactured scarcity ("only N spots").
- Must not contain the literal strings "taild1f9b7", "ts.net", or "?u=".
- No inline style="..." attributes (the validator rejects them) — put all CSS in the <style> block.
- The page must produce ZERO console errors when loaded.

ACCEPTANCE
The verifier `node verify.mjs` must exit 0 with all 30 checks passing. It runs html-validate for HTML5 validity and a headless Chromium against a local file:// URL for layout and console checks. It makes no network requests and needs no credentials.
Beyond the verifier, the copy quality matters: this page is read by strangers deciding whether to trust a solo project. Write real, specific, human prose — not marketing filler.

sprints.title: Skeleton, structure, and validity
sprints.description: Create index.html at repo root as a single self-contained file: <!doctype html>, <head> with meta charset + viewport, title, and an inline <style> block (system font stack only, no external requests). Build the six required <section> elements in exact document order with exact ids: hero, how-it-works, different, who, disclosure, signup. Use semantic HTML5 (header/main/section/footer). Populate real, specific human copy for every section per the positioning brief: hero leads on the OUTCOME (study without reading, study on a walk) with a one-sentence subhead and the verbatim tagline 'No cards. No quizzes. No flashcards. Just a conversation.'; how-it-works three one-line steps (upload a document -> talk through it out loud -> see what you actually covered); different as two short blocks (no-cards commitment + hands-free/phone-in-pocket, NO comparison table); who as one concrete paragraph (exams/interviews/new work domain/motivated self-learners; exclude note-taking & knowledge-management language); disclosure as full-size body trust copy (solo early project, runs on a machine in builder's apartment, uploads+transcripts stored & read by builder, voice passes through third-party speech/AI services). Avoid every forbidden string ('AI-native', 'service_role', 'taild1f9b7', 'ts.net', '?u='), no app links, no access token, no external URLs, no inline style attributes, no fake social proof/scarcity. Acceptance for this sprint: the file exists and passes html-validate HTML5 validity with zero errors (run node verify.mjs and confirm the HTML-validity and structural/id checks pass).

sprints.title: The signup form, duplicated and accessible
sprints.description: Add the email signup form in BOTH #hero and #signup. Each instance has two fields: a required Email input and an optional single-line free-text qualifying question labelled in plain language ('What's the one document you're trying to get into your head right now?'). Every input has a unique id and an associated <label for> pointing at it; because the form appears twice, guarantee ids are unique across the whole page (e.g. hero-email/hero-doc, signup-email/signup-doc) and give each form a submit button. Add an inline status/error region per form (aria-live) for later inline messaging. This is the only conversion action; do not link to the app. Acceptance: html-validate still passes, labels are correctly tied to inputs, all input ids unique, keyboard navigable — verified via node verify.mjs (accessibility/label/duplicate-id checks pass).

sprints.title: Supabase submit behaviour and inline states
sprints.description: Add the inline <script> that declares EXACTLY the two named constants once each with the exact given values (SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_KEY as plain string literals — no encoding/obfuscation, never reference service_role). Wire both forms to a shared submit handler that: does a basic client-side email format check with a clear inline error; disables the submit button BEFORE calling fetch (prevent double-insert); POSTs to SUPABASE_URL + '/rest/v1/signups' with headers apikey and Content-Type: application/json and body { email, document }; treats a 201/empty body as success by checking response.ok / status only (never reads the row back, never adds select=*, never parses body as success); renders success and error INLINE without navigating away; uses a real catch block; on network/API failure shows a plain message with a mailto: fallback and re-enables the button on the failure path. Ensure the Supabase REST call is the ONLY outbound http(s) URL in the entire file and the page throws ZERO console errors on load. Acceptance: node verify.mjs — console-error-free load and script-behaviour checks pass.

sprints.title: Responsive, theming, and final acceptance
sprints.description: Finalize the CSS in the <style> block: mobile-first layout that reads well at 375px and does not overflow horizontally at 375/768/1280px; visible focus states, adequate contrast, keyboard navigability; support both prefers-color-scheme light and dark; respect prefers-reduced-motion; keep the whole file under 50KB with system font stack only and no stock imagery/placeholders/lorem (CSS-only visuals if any). Confirm the disclosure section renders at full body size (not footer/modal/small text). Do a final pass removing any stray external URLs, inline style attributes, or forbidden strings. Acceptance: node verify.mjs exits 0 with all 30 checks passing across HTML validity, layout at all three widths, theming, and console cleanliness.
